PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Today, the Federal Home Loan Bank of Pittsburgh (FHLBank) joined Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh (RTP) alongside U.S. Rep. Summer Lee (D-PA-12), First Commonwealth Bank and stakeholders at a ribbon cutting for two Rehab for Resale (R4R) properties, located at 205 and 207 Rankin Blvd., as part of the Mon Valley Phase IV initiative.

In 2024-2025, FHLBank awarded nearly $5.7 million in Affordable Housing Program (AHP) and Voluntary Housing Grant (VHG) funding through its member financial institution, First Commonwealth Bank, to support RTP’s important rehabilitation efforts providing affordable homeownership opportunities throughout Mon Valley communities.

R4R Mon Valley Phase IV is an installment of a collaborative initiative between RTP, the Tri-COG Land Bank and First Commonwealth Bank to expand access to affordable homeownership in a region facing significant housing challenges.

“Increased access to quality, affordable housing is a core outcome of FHLBank’s dual mission,” said David G. Paulson, FHLBank president and CEO. “We are proud to support this initiative through multiple funding rounds of our Community Investment Products and are encouraged by the strong regional partnerships formed to not only preserve the existing housing supply, but also to create long-term wealth building opportunities and brighter futures for the families that will live here.”

The townhomes toured by event attendees today were two among six formerly vacant and blighted structures that Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh identified as opportunities to be restored into safe, healthy and affordable homes designated for buyers earning equal to or less than 80% of the area median income.

“We’re deeply grateful to FHLBank and our member bank, First Commonwealth Bank, for this partnership,” said Travis Renville, CEO, Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh. “Their support helps homeowners remain safely in the homes and communities they know and love, while allowing us to bring vacant homes back into use as safe, stable, and affordable places for new homeowners. By reducing blight, returning homes to the tax rolls, and welcoming new neighbors, this work helps strengthen communities in lasting ways.”

“We've got families across the Mon Valley who want to own a home, raise their kids, and build a future right here, but too often, the cost of housing puts that dream out of reach. Meanwhile, we've got vacant houses sitting in neighborhoods that deserve investment and a chance to thrive,” said Rep. Summer Lee. “I love seeing partners come together to give these homes new life and help working families build stability and generational wealth. I'm grateful to RTP, FHLBank, First Commonwealth Bank and everyone who helped make this happen, and I'm excited to see more of our neighbors get the opportunity to become homeowners.”

About FHLBank Pittsburgh

FHLBank Pittsburgh provides reliable funding and liquidity to its member financial institutions, which include commercial and savings banks, community development financial institutions, credit unions and insurance companies in Delaware, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. FHLBank products and resources help support community lending, housing and economic development. As one of 11 Federal Home Loan Banks established by Congress, FHLBank has been an integral and reliable part of the financial system since 1932. Learn more by visiting www.fhlb-pgh.com.

About Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh

Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh works to ensure everyone can live in a safe, healthy home. Since 1993, RTP has provided critical repairs for low- and moderate-income homeowners across the Pittsburgh region, helping residents remain safely housed, preserving affordable homeownership, and preventing homes from becoming vacant or blighted. Through its Rehab for Resale program, RTP also rehabilitates vacant homes and makes them affordable for income-qualified buyers, returning neglected properties to productive use and strengthening neighborhoods.

About First Commonwealth Financial Corporation

First Commonwealth Financial Corporation (NYSE: FCF), headquartered in Indiana, Pennsylvania, is a community bank committed to its mission of improving the financial lives of its neighbors and their businesses. First Commonwealth operates 126 branches throughout Pennsylvania and Ohio and also has business banking centers in Pittsburgh and Harrisburg, Pennsylvania; and Cleveland, Canton, Cincinnati and Columbus, Ohio. First Commonwealth, through subsidiaries First Commonwealth Bank and First Commonwealth Insurance Agency, provides a full range of commercial and retail banking services, including mortgage, wealth management and insurance solutions, along with equipment financing and SBA and indirect lending. For more information about First Commonwealth, visit www.fcbanking.com.

STOCKTON, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Health Net, one of California's most experienced Medi-Cal managed care health plans and company of Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC), today announced a $3 million investment in the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund. The funding will provide grants and low-interest loans to accelerate affordable housing developments and support the creation of at least 75 affordable homes for Stockton families facing some of the region's most significant housing challenges.

"A home is so much more than a roof overhead. It's the place where families feel safe, children can grow and learn, and people can focus on their health and well-being," said Dorothy M. Seleski, Medi-Cal Plan President at Health Net. "Too many families in our communities are struggling to find housing they can afford. By partnering with the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund, we're helping create more opportunities for families to put down roots, build stability and look toward the future with greater confidence. Together, we're investing in healthier communities by helping more people find a place to call home."

The investment will support community-driven housing developments, with a focus on serving families facing the greatest barriers to affordable housing, including households earning between 30% and 50% of the area median income.

"When local organizations unite around a shared goal, communities move forward," said San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund Board Chair Gary Singh. "Health Net's investment will help transform plans into homes for local families while encouraging broader community participation in addressing the region's housing needs."

The investment will support eligible projects through January 2029, from planning through construction.

"Investments in affordable housing are investments in the health, strength and future of our communities," said San Joaquin County Supervisor Robert Rickman. "By bringing public, private and community partners together, we can help more San Joaquin County families find stable housing and create lasting opportunity across the region."

In Sacramento and San Joaquin counties, Health Net has invested a combined $11 million in affordable housing and related initiatives, including $2 million to Stanislaus Equity Partners, Inc. (STEP) and $3 million to Fairview Terrace. By supporting developments at every stage, from planning and financing to construction and occupancy, Health Net is helping expand access to affordable housing, strengthen local communities and create the conditions for better health across the region.

About Health Net

Founded in California more than 45 years ago, Health Net, LLC ("Health Net"), a company of Centene Corporation, believes that every person deserves a safety net for their health, regardless of age, income, employment status or current state of health. Today, we provide health plans for individuals, families, businesses of every size and people who qualify for Medi-Cal or Medicare. With more than 117,000 of our network providers, Health Net serves more than three million members across the state. We also offer access to substance abuse programs, behavioral health services and managed healthcare products related to prescription drugs. We make these health plans and services available through Health Net and its subsidiaries: Health Net of California, Inc., Health Net Life Insurance Company and Health Net Community Solutions, Inc. These entities are wholly owned subsidiaries of Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC), a leading healthcare enterprise committed to transforming the health of the communities we serve, one person at a time. Health Net and Centene Corporation employ more than 5,700 people in California who work at one of five regional Talent Hub offices. For more information, visit www.HealthNet.com.

Both models are now available to order, with initial UK customer deliveries expected in January 2027 for the L03 and February 2027 for the G9L.

XPENG L03: next-generation AI SUV Coupé

The XPENG L03 is a next-generation AI SUV Coupé, combining SUV practicality with a supercar-inspired fastback silhouette and coupé proportions. Its “Vital Flow” design philosophy is expressed through a wide-body stance and frameless doors, giving the model a distinctive presence.

The UK launch range comprises Standard Range, Long Range, Long Range Ultra, AWD Performance and Power X Long Range (REEV) offering up to 323 miles of range for the BEV model and up to 631 miles for the Power X (REEV) version. DC charging from 20–80% takes approximately 20 minutes.

The G9L sits at the top of XPENG’s SUV range, with prices starting from £64,990 on the road for the Long Range 7-seater. The G9L will also offer an Ultra variant, equipped with hardware to support XPENG’s next-generation advanced driver assistance capabilities.

This makes it easier to navigate narrow streets and tight parking spaces. Power-folding third-row seats come as standard, offering greater flexibility for family journeys, business travel and everyday use.

Premium comfort is another highlight of the G9L, with a built-in 12.5L refrigerator, a 21.4-inch 3K entertainment screen and a 23-speaker surround sound system as standard. Together with its spacious and a child-centric cabin, these features deliver a refined experience for drivers and passengers alike.

Safety is also central to the G9L’s design. Engineered to meet the requirements of four global five-star safety assessment programmes, covering 113 test protocols, the G9L comes with up to 10 airbags. It also features a tyre blowout stability control system designed to help maintain vehicle stability in the event of a sudden tyre failure.

An exciting step for XPENG UK

“Bringing the XPENG G9L and XPENG L03 to the UK gives customers greater choice, with our two latest SUVs offering advanced technology, strong specifications and compelling value at their respective price points,” said James Cowan, Marketing Director of XPENG UK, “The flagship G9L combines comfort, capability and intelligent features, while the L03 offers a fresh SUV Coupé design and an accessible entry point to the XPENG range.”

WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / A Strategic Opportunity in a Changing Energy Landscape

Lithium remains an important material in the lithium-ion batteries used across electric vehicles and energy-storage applications. As manufacturers, policymakers and investors continue to focus on resilient supply chains, the development of reliable North American sources remains an important industry theme.

ELEKTROS Inc. (OTC PINK:ELEK), a publicly traded company on the OTC market, is evaluating a potential hard-rock lithium opportunity in northern New York, near the Canadian border on the American side. The opportunity remains exploratory. ELEKTROS has not announced a completed acquisition, independently verified mineral resource or reserve, or a determination that the property can be developed economically.

The Potential Advantage of a Domestic Location

A U.S.-based source of lithium, if supported by geology, property rights, permitting, infrastructure and commercially viable economics, could offer a more direct route to domestic processing customers. Depending on the project's eventual development pathway, domestic transportation could potentially reduce reliance on overseas ocean freight and certain international customs and import-related procedures.

These potential benefits have not been established for the property under review. A domestic location by itself does not establish mineral quality, project economics, permitting feasibility or commercial success.

Industry Demand Underscores the Importance of Supply

In an October 22, 2026 article titled "Lithium's $100 Billion Supply Gap Hands Albemarle a Domestic Moat," Benzinga reported a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence outlook that global lithium demand could more than triple by 2050, potentially requiring 134 new mines and more than $100 billion in investment. The article also discussed demand associated with electric vehicles and stationary battery storage.

Those figures are industry-wide estimates and are not forecasts for ELEKTROS or the northern New York opportunity. The Benzinga article discussed other companies, not ELEKTROS.

Lithium Interests and EV Charging Technology

In addition to evaluating lithium opportunities, ELEKTROS continues to explore potential development relationships involving its multi-port EV charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company views domestic lithium sourcing and EV charging innovation as separate but complementary areas of long-term interest.

No commercial charging prototype, licensing arrangement, customer adoption or patent-related revenue is being announced in this release.

The Milestones That Matter

The next meaningful steps in evaluating the northern New York opportunity include confirming property and mineral rights; obtaining independent geological assessment and sampling; reviewing environmental, land-use and permitting requirements; identifying realistic processing and transportation pathways; and evaluating potential financing needs and transaction terms.

ELEKTROS believes that a careful, evidence-based review is essential to determining whether the opportunity can progress beyond an early-stage concept. Any future decision would depend on the results of due diligence and the company's assessment of the associated risks, costs and potential benefits.

A Message to Shareholders

ELEKTROS appreciates the continued interest of its shareholders and those following the evolving North American lithium supply chain. The company intends to evaluate potential opportunities with ambition, discipline and respect for the technical, regulatory and financial work required to advance an early-stage project.

Management expresses gratitude to Almighty God as the company works toward measurable progress. This news release is provided for informational purposes only; it is not an offer to sell securities or a recommendation to purchase ELEK shares.

ELEKTROS Inc. is a publicly traded company on the OTC market under ticker symbol ELEK. Its areas of interest include hard-rock lithium opportunities, EV charging infrastructure and patented EV charging technology. The potential northern New York property discussed in this release has not been acquired by ELEKTROS and is not a producing mine.

Report finds North American market rents average about 6% below the rent needed to justify new construction, as the global office pipeline falls 41% from its peak

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cushman & Wakefield (NYSE: CWK), a leading global real estate services firm, today released Global Office Supply: The Development Drought, finding that North American market rents averaged $77.03 per square foot (psf) in 2026, about 6% below the economic rent, which is the minimum rent a new office development needs to earn to be profitable. The report projects that average market rents will not catch up until the early 2030s.

Globally, the under-construction office pipeline stood at 580 million square feet (msf) in Q3 2026, 45% below its 2017 peak and its lowest level in a decade. The report attributes the decline to “higher for longer” interest rates, sharply higher construction costs and an investor pivot away from the office sector. In North America, economic rents overtook market rents in 2023, when construction costs rose by double digits and borrowing costs began to climb.

“Demand for high-quality, well-located space is resurging just as the supply pipeline is drying up,” said Sandy Romero, Head of Office & Alternatives Insights at Cushman & Wakefield. “Average rents have not kept pace with the cost of building, so in most North American markets new supply will have to be built with the quality and amenities required to get leading rents in order to pencil out. Existing top-tier space is being absorbed faster than it can be replaced, which is driving rent growth in that segment, as well as more lease renewals and earlier occupier searches.”

New York is the clear outlier among the markets analyzed. Market rents of $156.64 psf in 2026 were nearly 60% above the economic rent of $98.69 psf, and New York has already begun to see construction tick up, with 6.4 msf underway as of Q3 2026, nearly double the level from a year ago. More than 2.5 msf of office space is under renovation as owners respond to the flight to quality.

Elsewhere, the viability gap varies. Chicago has the widest near-term gap among the U.S. markets analyzed, with 2026 market rents of $84.56 psf, 10% below the economic rent of $93.75 psf, and Class A vacancy of 24.0%. Boston market rents of $78.59 psf were 8% below economic rent, and the market currently has no projects under construction or renovation. San Francisco is close to the threshold, at 4% below economic rent ($98.43 psf versus $102.94 psf), with strong demand from AI occupiers expected to drive a recovery even as Class A vacancy remains high at 31.1%. Boston and San Francisco are both projected to reach viability in 2029, while Chicago is not projected to do so until 2032. Given the typical timeline to develop a new office building is three to five years, these thresholds are not as far out as they may initially seem.

In Canada, the report forecasts market and economic rents converging in Toronto around 2031, with no new development currently expected to commence before 2032. Downtown Class A and AAA vacancy stands at 10%, falling to 7.1% in the Financial Core. In Vancouver, which recently completed its largest office delivery cycle on record, roughly 3.8 msf across ten towers between 2020 and 2024, metro vacancy rose to 11.8% in Q3 2026, the highest rate since the early 2000s. The report forecasts economic rent will exceed market rent there through 2035.

“For occupiers, limited new supply means rising competition for top-tier space, so planning well ahead of lease events matters more than ever,” Romero said. “For investors and developers, new starts are likely to remain selective. In the meantime, we expect more renovations of existing buildings and more build-to-suit projects, particularly in markets where demand for brand new space is already building.”

The report also analyzes development viability across APAC and EMEA, using a consistent economic rent framework that accounts for land, construction, operating, leasing and financing costs and developer margin, and offers strategies for occupiers, investors, developers and owners.

For additional insights and analysis, read the full Global Office Supply: The Development Drought report.

The software represents a significant new step in delivering automated, scalable traffic management solutions for Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) across Brazil and worldwide.

Designed with a modular and scalable architecture, Vector features Helipad and Vertiport (Aerodrome) and Ground Operations modules, enabling operators to seamlessly manage high-volume activities across vertiports and helipads. Key Terms

cold rolledtechnical
A metalworking process in which metal (commonly steel or aluminum) is passed through rollers at or near room temperature to reduce thickness and produce a smoother, more precise surface and tighter dimensional tolerances. Because the work is done below the metal’s recrystallization temperature, cold rolling increases strength and hardness through strain hardening but also reduces ductility; the metal is often annealed afterwards to restore formability if further shaping is required.
galvanized productstechnical
Galvanized products are metal items—most often steel or iron—whose exposed surfaces have been coated with a layer of zinc to protect them from rust and corrosion. The zinc coating is applied either by hot-dip galvanizing (immersing the metal in molten zinc) or by electro-galvanizing (using an electrical process to deposit zinc), and it protects the base metal both by creating a physical barrier and by sacrificing itself chemically if the surface is scratched. Different galvanizing methods produce coatings with different thicknesses and durability, so galvanized does not mean permanently corrosion-proof but indicates enhanced resistance compared with uncoated metal.

Participation in Oracle Health Information Network will help clinicians access more complete health information and support coordinated care for Veterans, service members, and other beneficiaries

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle Health announced that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Department of War (DoW) began participating in Oracle Health Information Network, a designated Qualified Health Information Network® (QHIN™) under the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement™ (TEFCA®) on November 5, 2026. By participating in Oracle Health Information Network, clinicians will have increased access to health information from participating healthcare organizations nationwide, improving care coordination and care for Veterans and service members.

Participation in Oracle Health Information Network will build on the existing Joint Health Information Exchange (JHIE) and give VA and DoW clinicians access to a broader range of patient information from participating community providers and other healthcare organizations. Over time, this may include additional information such as medical images, medications, and other data that may not be as readily available today. Clinicians can review and, when appropriate, reconcile that information into the patient chart using Oracle Health Seamless Exchange to limit duplicate information. This centralized and more complete view of a patient's health history supports better-informed care decisions, can help reduce unnecessary duplicate testing and clinical procedures, and enables more coordinated care for Veterans and service members.

VA and DoW serve millions of Veterans, service members, and other beneficiaries who receive care across federal and community healthcare settings. Through Oracle Health Information Network, VA and DoW will be able to securely exchange health information with organizations participating in TEFCA, extending their nationwide connectivity and helping make relevant health information available to clinicians as patients move across care settings.

Oracle Health Information Network provides a single connection point for secure information exchange across a broad range of healthcare organizations and use cases. This approach reduces the need to establish and maintain separate connections with individual organizations and provides a foundation for broader collaboration across care settings. As a designated QHIN, Oracle Health Information Network also enables nationwide exchange with organizations connected through TEFCA.

Oracle Health invites healthcare providers across the country to connect through Oracle Health Information Network to support the care of Veterans, service members, and beneficiaries. Broader participation can help clinicians across federal and community settings access the information they need to deliver more informed, coordinated care wherever these patients seek treatment.

"Delivering the best possible care for Veterans and civilian and military personnel starts with giving clinicians a comprehensive picture of their health," said Seema Verma, executive vice president and general manager, Oracle Health and Life Sciences. "We are honored to continue working with VA and DoW to advance their interoperability goals through Oracle Health Information Network, which gives clinicians timely access to critical health information wherever Veterans and DoW personnel receive care. This is another important step toward a connected healthcare system that puts patients first."

Japan Patent Office allows claims directed to xanthine oxidase inhibitor compositions for acute kidney injury and other health consequences of viral infection; once registered, patent expected to remain in force until March 2041

CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XORTX Therapeutics Inc. (“XORTX” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: XRTX), a late-stage clinical pharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative therapies to treat gout and progressive kidney disease, is pleased to announce that the Japan Patent Office (the “JPO”) has issued a Decision to Grant a Patent for Japanese Patent Application No. 2022-556140, entitled “Compositions, Formulations, and Containers” (the “Japanese Patent”). Once registered, the Japanese Patent will support the Company’s XRx-101 program for acute kidney injury and other acute organ injury associated with respiratory virus infections, and will be the Company’s first patent in Japan directed to its xanthine oxidase inhibitor programs.

A Decision to Grant is the JPO’s determination that the examiner has found no reasons to refuse the application. The Japanese Patent will issue upon payment of the registration fee and registration by the JPO. The application is the Japanese national phase of International Application No. PCT/IB2021/000238 and claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/989,879, filed March 15, 2020. The six allowed claims are directed to pharmaceutical compositions comprising a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, including oxypurinol, for the treatment or prevention of acute kidney injury and other health consequences associated with viral infection. Under Japanese patent practice, therapeutic uses are generally protected through composition claims. Once registered, the Japanese Patent is expected to remain in force until March 15, 2041, subject to the payment of annuity fees and excluding any patent term extension that may become available

“This decision is expected to provide XRx-101 with its first patent protection in Japan, one of the world’s largest pharmaceutical markets, and the allowed claims are directed to the central premise of the program – that inhibiting xanthine oxidase may attenuate injurious, rapid increases in uric acid and the acute kidney injury that can follow serious respiratory viral infection,” stated Dr. Allen Davidoff, Co-Chief Executive Officer of XORTX, who added, “Expanding our xanthine oxidase inhibitor patent estate into Japan strengthens the intellectual property position of that platform, which also includes XORLO™ for gout, and broadens the options available to the Company as it evaluates potential partnering opportunities for programs beyond XRx-026.”

Including the Japanese Patent, XORTX’s portfolio includes seven granted or allowed patents and 14 pending patent applications in the United States, Europe and Japan covering compositions and uses of xanthine oxidase inhibitors for gout, the health consequences of hyperuricemia, progressive kidney disease and acute kidney injury, together with approximately 30 patents acquired with the VB4-P5 renal anti-fibrotic program. The Company has not entered into any partnering, licensing or other agreement with any party regarding XRx-101, and there can be no assurance that it will enter into any such agreement on acceptable terms, or at all. XORTX looks forward to providing further updates as it continues to build its intellectual property portfolio and advances programs to treat patients with acute and chronic progressive disease.

About XORTX Therapeutics Inc.

XORTX is a pharmaceutical company with three clinically advanced products in development: 1) our lead XRx-026 program for the treatment of gout; 2) XRx-008 program for ADPKD; and 3) XRx-101 for acute kidney and other acute organ injury associated with respiratory virus infections. In addition, the Company is developing XRx-225, a pre-clinical stage program for Type 2 diabetic nephropathy, and the recently acquired VB4-P5 program, which is currently at the pre-IND stage of development and targets both rare and prevalent forms of kidney disease. XORTX is working to advance products that target aberrant purine metabolism and xanthine oxidase to decrease or inhibit production of uric acid. At XORTX, we are dedicated to developing medications that improve the quality of life and health of individuals with gout and other important diseases.

Alphen aan den Rijn, NL – November 13, 2026 – Wolters Kluwer Health has signed an agreement to acquire AgileMD, a healthcare technology company, for up to $100 million, of which $40 million is an upfront payment and the balance is a deferred consideration contingent upon reaching certain performance targets.

AgileMD provides AI-powered clinical decision support for health care professionals, offering them interactive clinical pathways and predictive analytics to enhance consistency in care and help them to reduce mortality rates. The company’s Pathways product operationalizes local guidelines in the EHR workflow for consistency in care and outcomes measurement. Its eCART solution is a real-time AI-powered clinical surveillance engine that is FDA1-cleared and designed to help reduce mortality rates.

“Combined with UpToDate Expert AI and our partnerships, AgileMD will serve as a vital enabler for true UpToDate ubiquity in healthcare – facilitating UpToDate’s expansion into embedded workflows, local guidelines, and new digital health applications,” said Yaw Fellin, Senior Vice President, Wolters Kluwer Clinical Solutions. “With AgileMD, we are well positioned to help healthcare systems provide better patient care and extract more value from their tech investments.”

Borna Safabakhsh, Co-Founder and CEO at AgileMD, commented, “We are excited to join Wolters Kluwer Health. Coupled with UpToDate, AgileMD can more fully deliver its transformative impact in critical decision support workflows. Leveraging UpToDate’s foundational capabilities, AgileMD will accelerate and streamline the development and maintenance of more advanced clinical pathways for complex clinical decision-making support.”

Since its introduction in September 2025, UpToDate Expert AI has been adopted by more than 2,700 U.S. hospitals and health systems, representing more than 95% of U.S.-based UpToDate Enterprise Edition customers.

Additional information and financial terms

AgileMD, based in San Francisco, was founded in 2011 and is currently led by co-founders Borna Safabakhsh and Dana Edelson, M.D., Chief Medical Officer. All 23 employees will be joining Wolters Kluwer Health. AgileMD has seen strong growth and is expected to reach annual recurring revenues (ARR) of $7 million by year-end 2026. The acquisition is expected to achieve a return on invested capital (ROIC) at or above our after-tax weighted average cost of capital (WACC) of 8% within 3-5 years and to have an immaterial impact on Wolters Kluwer adjusted earnings. The transaction, which is subject to customary closing conditions and other governmental approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 or sooner.
